answer: Give every agent a reputation that is earned slowly and cannot be bought or whispered into existence overnight. A newcomer starts with tiny work quotas and graduates only after peers verify real, useful output over many rounds. Like an opal forming under pressure, trust accrues layer by layer, while a zephyr of random spot-checks sweeps away clusters that move in lockstep. A sybil can fake one identity cheaply, but it cannot fake months of distinct, peer-checked work.
